purpose: Persistent visual QA memory for Instagram Stories/Reels. Reuse approved visual language and avoid previously observed defects.

brand_language.palette: deep navy/black with restrained blue/cyan accents
brand_language.lighting: cinematic but physically plausible, mostly cool with controlled warm practical light
brand_language.composition: premium, minimal, mobile-safe, strong subject hierarchy, safe top/bottom UI areas
brand_language.texture: real materials, subtle imperfections, no plastic CGI sheen
brand_language.motion: slow natural camera movement; no impossible physics

preferred_story_moods: clean workspace + coffee + subtle screen glow
must_check: opening frame reads immediately on a phone
no warped hands/devices or broken screens
no duplicated objects or impossible reflections
text is sharp and inside Instagram-safe areas
audio is clean, low-volume, and appropriate
visual motion is subtle and physically believable
subject/materials look photographic rather than synthetic
no accidental brand logos or unsupported product claims
known_bad_patterns: external image hotlinks that fail in render environments
complex procedural FFmpeg audio graphs causing render failures
overly strong zoom or artificial motion
generic neon-tech CGI without believable materials

steps: inspect full frame and representative motion frames
score realism, composition, text, motion, audio and technical accuracy
repeat until the candidate clears the publish threshold or the verified free-route budget is exhausted
save the approved recipe and defect notes for future runs

approved_recipe_notes: Prefer generated or uploaded stable media over fragile third-party hotlinks.
Use native Instagram audio only when the publisher can resolve the exact audio safely; otherwise use original/allowed audio.
Use Higgsfield video analysis for short generated clips when available to support scene-by-scene QA.
Use Canva for cover/text hierarchy QA when a design asset is involved.
Use Context7 for current technical facts and documentation when the content is technical.
